claim.why_it_matters: Sibling clauses at the same numeric depth are transcribed at different markdown heading levels, so the outline/TOC nesting is wrong: D.14.3.2.3 renders as a peer of D.14.3.2 instead of a child of it, and D.14.3.3 as a peer of D.14.3 instead of a child. Any tool that derives clause structure (TOC, anchor generation, citation depth) from heading level mis-parents these clauses. The same defect recurs in this batch at '## D.14.3.4' (p1117), '## D.14.3.5' and '## D.14.3.6' (p1118), '## D.14.4' (p1119) and '## D.16.5' (p1124); the pattern across the whole file is that only the FIRST subclause under a parent keeps its correct level and every later sibling is promoted to '##' (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 44889, 44898, 44949, 44999, 45024, 45047, 45179).

verdict.reasoning: REJECTED. Nothing is missing or altered on page 1116; the alleged defect is markdown heading markup over text that is fully and correctly present, and the claim's account of both the PDF and the pattern is wrong. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. Filed as kind=missing-heading, but both headings are present verbatim, in the right order, in the right place: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 44889 '## D.14.3.2.3 Switching locales outside of COBOL' and line 44898 '## D.14.3.3 Locale-based monetary and numeric formatting'. Rendered page 1116 (E:/Temp/specrecon/v1116/spec_p1116.png) prints exactly those two headings and no others. Clause numbers, titles and the full body prose of both clauses match the render: the SET LOCALE LC_ALL TO USER-DEFAULT example, the '01 US-amount PICTURE +$9.9 LOCALE SIZE IS 10.' example, the LC_MONETARY paragraph, the SPECIAL-NAMES/my-locale fragment, and the trailing 'Multiple locales may be used' sentence are all reproduced exactly. The rejection criterion 'the missing text is actually present' fires directly. The only difference anywhere on this page is the count of '#' characters. (2) THE PDF PRINTS NO DEPTH CUE, SO NO TYPOGRAPHIC SIGNAL WAS LOST. I measured this myself. The PDF text layer is obfuscated (page index 1115 decodes to U+0200-range junk and cannot be string-matched), so the headings must be identified geometrically; doing that with PyMuPDF gives, for every bold heading span regardless of clause depth, the identical font, size and left margin -- Cambria,Bold 11.67pt at x0=63.5. On PDF index 1113 (= markdown 'Page 1114'): y0=393.7 'D.14.3.2 Locale selection' (3 numeric levels), y0=419.0 'D.14.3.2.1 General' (4 levels), y0=608.6 'D.14.3.2.2 Switching locales in a COBOL runtime module' (4 levels). On PDF index 1115 (= markdown 'Page 1116'): y0=128.1 'D.14.3.2.3 ...' (4 levels) and y0=267.2 'D.14.3.3 ...' (3 levels). Same face, same 11.67pt size, same flush-left x0=63.5, same spacing -- for 3-level and 4-level clauses alike. The 300dpi renders of pp.1114/1116 confirm this visually: I looked at the printed glyphs and there is no size, weight, or indentation difference between a 3-level and a 4-level Annex D heading. The claim's phrase 'both printed at the same clause depth as their siblings' therefore describes the NUMBERING, not anything the page prints; the PDF encodes depth solely in the dotted-decimal number, and the markdown reproduces that number verbatim, so depth remains deterministically recoverable ('D.14.3.2.3' -> depth 5). Zero information present in the PDF is absent from the markdown. (3) THE CLAIMED PATTERN IS FALSE. The claim asserts 'only the FIRST subclause under a parent keeps its correct level and every later sibling is promoted to ##'. Three independent counterexamples, all verified: D.16.1 (45085), D.16.2 (45090), D.16.3 (45095) and D.16.4 (45100) are ALL '###' -- four consecutive siblings, every one keeping its level; D.14.3.2.1 (44804) and D.14.3.2.2 (44817) are BOTH '###'; D.14.2.1 (44705) and D.14.2.2 (44714) are BOTH '####'. So it is not 'every later sibling'. The actual mechanism is page-scoped level assignment: within each transcribed page slice the shallowest heading is emitted as '##' and deeper headings on that same page nest below it, and the numbering resets at every page boundary. D.14.2.3 is '##' because it opens the page-1113 slice; D.14.3.2.3 is '##' because it opens the page-1116 slice, and D.14.3.3 is '##' because it is shallower than the '##' already consumed on that page. That makes this a global property of the transcription pipeline that would fire on hundreds of pages -- page-break furniture, an explicit reject category -- not a page-1116 discrepancy. (4) THE 'WHY IT MATTERS' RATIONALE IS FALSE ON ITS OWN TERMS. Heading level is nowhere in this file a clause outline. The transcription emits the page running header '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' as an H1 941 times and the page marker '## Page NNNN' as an H2 1233 times, out of 947 total H1 and 2304 total H2 in the whole file. Any tool deriving clause structure from heading level would already be swamped by 1233 'Page NNNN' H2 nodes and 941 identical H1 running headers and would mis-parent essentially every clause in the document, entirely independently of p1116. Heading level here is page-transcription furniture; clause structure comes from the clause number, which is intact. Anchor generation and citation are likewise unaffected: the markdown supplies explicit stable anchors immediately above both headings, '' and ''. (5) WHAT IS TRUE, AND WHY IT STILL DOES NOT QUALIFY. The bare observation is verifiable: numeric siblings do carry different '#' counts (D.14.3.2.1/.2 are '###' while D.14.3.2.3 is '##'; D.14.3.1 is '###' while D.14.3.3 is '##'), and that does diverge from the PDF's own bookmark tree. But it is markdown formatting over text that is fully present, it changes no meaning, it drops no fact recoverable from the page, and depth stays exactly derivable from the clause number -- which is the citation form this project actually uses. Both explicit rejection criteria ('the difference is only ... formatting' and 'the difference does not change meaning') apply. Annex D is informative, and no normative or informative statement is affected. real=false.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a page-1116 PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy. Both headings are transcribed verbatim with correct clause numbers, titles and body text, and both already carry explicit section anchors. The PDF prints every Annex D clause heading identically regardless of depth -- measured geometrically (the text layer is obfuscated and cannot be string-matched) as Cambria,Bold 11.67pt at x0=63.5 for the 3-level D.14.3.2 and D.14.3.3 as well as the 4-level D.14.3.2.1, D.14.3.2.2 and D.14.3.2.3 -- so there was no printed depth cue to lose; depth lives only in the dotted number, which is preserved. The residual observation -- that markdown '#' counts do not track clause depth -- is a real but purely cosmetic, file-wide property of the transcription, and the claim mis-states its cause: levels are assigned per page slice (the shallowest heading on a page becomes '##', deeper ones nest below it) and reset at each page boundary, NOT 'only the first subclause keeps its level'. That rule is disproved by D.16.1-D.16.4 (all '###'), D.14.3.2.1/D.14.3.2.2 (both '###') and D.14.2.1/D.14.2.2 (both '####'). The stated impact is also unfounded, since heading level is never a clause outline in this file (941 H1 running headers and 1233 '## Page NNNN' H2 markers). If tracked at all, this belongs as a single global transcription-pipeline note in a cosmetic markup-normalization backlog, not as a per-page structural finding in the spec-reconciliation ledger.
